UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile and personalized settings within the CaptionWise application. This entity stores user-specific configurations like theme preferences, but excludes sensitive authentication data handled by an external system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

themePreference.description: The user's preferred application theme (e.g., 'light' or 'dark').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

Image.title: Image
Image.description: Represents an image uploaded by a user to the CaptionWise application for caption generation. It stores metadata about the image and its storage location.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Image entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who uploaded this image. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Image)

imageUrl.description: The URL where the uploaded image is stored (e.g., in cloud storage).

fileName.description: The original file name of the uploaded image as provided by the user.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the uploaded image (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png').

sizeBytes.description: The size of the uploaded image in bytes.

uploadedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the image was uploaded.

CaptionSuggestion.title: CaptionSuggestion
CaptionSuggestion.description: Represents a caption suggested for an image, which can be initially generated by AI and subsequently refined by a user. Multiple suggestions can exist for a single image.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CaptionSuggestion entity.

imageId.description: Reference to the Image for which this caption was suggested. (Relationship: Image 1:N CaptionSuggestion)

text.description: The actual text content of the caption suggestion or its refined version.

isUserRefined.description: A flag indicating whether this caption suggestion has been refined or modified by the user since its initial generation.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the caption was initially generated or suggested by the AI.

lastModifiedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the caption was last modified, either by a re-generation from AI or by user refinement.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and QAPs (Query-Accessible Paths) by leveraging a strictly hierarchical, user-owned data model. Each user's data is isolated within their specific path, making security rules simple, robust, and easy to debug.

1.  **User Profile (`/users/{userId}`):** User profiles are stored directly under `/users/{userId}`. This path-based ownership means that the `userId` in the document path directly corresponds to `request.auth.uid` for authorization. This is inherently secure for single-document reads and writes, as well as listing operations, since a user can only query their own path.

2.  **Images (`/users/{userId}/images/{imageId}`):** Images uploaded by a user are stored as a subcollection of their user profile. This structure ensures that every `Image` document inherently includes the `userId` in its path. This design is crucial for **Authorization Independence** because the ownership context (who owns the image) is explicitly part of the document's location. Security rules can directly check `request.auth.uid == userId` without needing to perform a `get()` operation on the parent user document or requiring the `Image` document itself to contain an `ownerId` field (though including `userId` as a field within the `Image` document is still good practice for indexing and data integrity, it's not strictly necessary for authorization independence *if* the path is always used). This also supports **QAPs** effectively: a user can only list images within their own `/users/{request.auth.uid}/images` path, making all list queries inherently secure and pre-filtered.

3.  **Caption Suggestions (`/users/{userId}/images/{imageId}/captionSuggestions/{captionSuggestionId}`):** Caption suggestions are nested one level deeper, under the specific image they belong to. This further extends the hierarchical ownership model. The full path contains both the `userId` and `imageId`, ensuring that a `CaptionSuggestion` is always tied to a specific image owned by a specific user. This adheres to **Authorization Independence** as the `userId` in the path is sufficient for authorization rules, avoiding any `get()` calls to parent `Image` or `UserProfile` documents. For **QAPs**, listing caption suggestions is secure by default: a user can only list suggestions for images they own, as all queries must include their `request.auth.uid` in the path. The structure ensures that all documents at a given path have a homogeneous security posture (private to the `userId` in the path), simplifying rules dramatically.

By embedding the `userId` directly into the path for all user-specific data, we achieve complete Authorization Independence, eliminate `get()` calls in security rules, and ensure that all `list` operations are securely pre-filtered by the path, adhering to the QAPs principle.
